description: Multiply your projector's throw ratio (or zoom range) by screen width to get the exact throw-distance range in feet and metres.

faqs.a: Throw ratio = throw distance ÷ screen width. A 1.5:1 projector must sit 1.5 × the screen width away — for a 100-inch-wide screen that is 150 inches.
The shortest throw ratio in the zoom range gives the closest mounting position; the longest gives the farthest. Mount the projector between those distances and use zoom to fine-tune.
faqs.q: How do I use the min/max distance range?

faqs.a: Yes — the tool derives width from a 16:9 diagonal, or you can type the screen width directly if you know it.
faqs.q: Can I enter screen width directly?

howto: Enter your screen size (16:9 diagonal) or type the screen width directly.
Enter the projector's throw ratio, or the min/max of its zoom range.
Read the throw distance (or range) in feet and metres for mounting.
title: Projector Throw Calculator
